topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes, references previous histopathology practicals, and outlines the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, proto-oncogenes, and cell transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the discovery of viral and cellular oncogenes from early cell and germ theories to retroviral capture of proto-oncogenes and experimental assays for transformed cell phenotypes.

topics.label: Functional classes of cancer mutations and cell cycle checkpoint regulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the classification of oncogenes and tumor suppressors, illustrating their dosage and mechanistic effects through the Rb G1/S checkpoint and dominant-negative p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of sequence and chromosomal instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability, detailing how defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate genomic abnormalities in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations drives tumorigenesis across clinical syndromes and tumor progression models.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the session, offers recommended reading, and provides housekeeping for the next lecture.
